title: Vapour Compression Refrigeration (VCR) Demonstration Rig
disclaimer: Educational visualisation generated procedurally for this project. It is not a CAD model, is not dimensionally exact and does not represent a specific commercial product. Items marked 'illustrative' are typical accessories shown for teaching.

labData.note: Editable placeholders. Replace with values measured on your laboratory rig. Nothing here is a measured result.
labData.refrigerant: [refrigerant type — to be filled from rig nameplate]

stages.title: Evaporation (heat absorbed)
stages.text: Cold, low-pressure liquid–vapour mixture enters the evaporator. It absorbs heat from the space or product being cooled and boils into low-pressure vapour.
stages.ideal: Ideal cycle: constant-pressure heat addition until the refrigerant is saturated vapour.
stages.real: Real systems: a small pressure drop occurs across the coil and the vapour is usually slightly superheated at the outlet so that no liquid reaches the compressor.

stages.title: Compression (work input)
stages.text: The compressor draws in the low-pressure vapour and squeezes it into high-pressure, high-temperature vapour, using electrical work input.
stages.real: Real systems: friction, heat transfer and valve losses make the compression non-isentropic, so more work is needed than in the ideal cycle.

stages.title: Condensation (heat rejected)
stages.text: Hot, high-pressure vapour gives up heat to the surrounding air through the condenser fins, cools and condenses into high-pressure liquid.
stages.ideal: Ideal cycle: constant-pressure heat rejection to saturated liquid.
stages.real: Real systems: the liquid is often slightly subcooled at the outlet, and there is a small frictional pressure drop.

stages.title: Expansion (throttling)
stages.text: The high-pressure liquid is forced through a restriction. Its pressure falls sharply, part of it flashes into vapour, and its temperature drops before it re-enters the evaporator.
stages.ideal: Ideal cycle: irreversible throttling at constant enthalpy (no work, no heat transfer).
stages.real: Real systems: very close to constant enthalpy; a thermostatic expansion valve also adjusts flow to keep evaporator-outlet superheat roughly steady.

components.name: Compressor
components.subtitle: Hermetic reciprocating/rotary type (shown schematically)
components.function: Draws in low-pressure refrigerant vapour from the evaporator and raises its pressure and temperature so it can reject heat in the condenser.
components.principle: Mechanical work from an electric motor sealed inside the shell reduces the volume of the vapour, raising its pressure; the temperature rises with it.
components.cycleRole: The 'pump' of the cycle: it creates the pressure difference between the high side and the low side and keeps refrigerant circulating.
components.application: Domestic refrigerators, window/split air-conditioners, water coolers and cold rooms all use a compressor of this kind.
components.student: Think of it as the heart of the fridge: it pumps refrigerant around and squeezes it so it gets hot enough to dump heat outside.

components.name: Condenser
components.subtitle: Air-cooled finned-tube coil
components.function: Rejects heat from the refrigerant to the surroundings and condenses high-pressure vapour into liquid.
components.principle: Hot vapour flows through copper tubes; heat conducts into the aluminium fins and is carried away by air driven by the condenser fan. Removing latent heat turns the vapour into liquid at nearly constant pressure.
components.cycleRole: Heat rejection: removes the heat absorbed in the evaporator plus the compressor work.
components.application: The warm coil at the back of a fridge or the outdoor unit of a split air-conditioner.
components.student: This is where the heat taken out of the fridge is thrown away — that is why the back of a fridge feels warm.

components.name: Expansion Device
components.subtitle: Thermostatic expansion valve with sensing bulb (a capillary tube is a common alternative)
components.function: Throttles the refrigerant, reducing its pressure and generally its temperature, and meters the flow into the evaporator.
components.principle: Liquid is forced through a small orifice. The sudden pressure drop makes part of the liquid flash into vapour, which cools the remaining mixture. In a thermostatic valve, a bulb on the suction line moves a diaphragm to open or close the orifice to control superheat.
components.cycleRole: Separates the high-pressure side from the low-pressure side and controls how much refrigerant enters the evaporator.
components.application: Capillary tubes in household refrigerators; thermostatic or electronic expansion valves in air-conditioners and cold storage.
components.student: Like spraying an aerosol can: the pressure drops suddenly and the spray feels cold.

components.name: Evaporator
components.subtitle: Finned-tube coil (blue-tinted fins used here only to tell it apart)
components.function: Absorbs heat from the space or product being cooled and vaporises the low-pressure refrigerant.
components.principle: Low-pressure refrigerant boils at a low temperature. Air blown across the fins by the evaporator fan is warmer than the refrigerant, so heat flows into the refrigerant and supplies its latent heat of vaporisation.
components.cycleRole: Produces the refrigerating effect — this is where the useful cooling happens.
components.application: The cold plate or freezer coil in a refrigerator; the indoor coil of an air-conditioner.
components.student: The refrigerant 'boils' here while still cold, soaking up heat from the food or room — that is the cooling you feel.

components.name: Receiver / Filter-Drier
components.subtitle: Illustrative accessory with sight glass
components.function: Stores surplus liquid refrigerant and removes moisture and particles before the expansion device.
components.principle: A desiccant core adsorbs water and a mesh filter traps dirt; the sight glass lets technicians check for a full liquid column.
components.outlet: Clean, dry high-pressure liquid to the expansion device
components.cycleRole: Protects the expansion device from blockage and the system from moisture.
components.application: Common in air-conditioning and commercial refrigeration systems.
components.student: A water filter for the refrigerant: it keeps the tiny valve from clogging.

components.name: Condenser Fan
components.subtitle: Axial fan and motor
components.function: Forces ambient air through the condenser coil to carry heat away.
components.principle: Forced convection increases the rate of heat transfer from the fins to the air.
components.cycleRole: Supports heat rejection at the condenser.
components.application: Outdoor units of air-conditioners, fan-cooled condensing units.
components.student: A fan that blows the heat away from the hot coil.

components.name: Evaporator Fan
components.subtitle: Axial fan and motor
components.function: Circulates air from the cooled space across the evaporator coil.
components.principle: Forced convection increases heat transfer from the air to the cold fins.
components.inlet: Warm air from the cooled space
components.cycleRole: Supports heat absorption at the evaporator and distributes the cooling.
components.application: Frost-free refrigerators, indoor units of split air-conditioners, cold rooms.
components.student: It pushes room air over the cold coil so the cold spreads around.

components.name: Discharge Line
components.subtitle: Copper tube, compressor → condenser
components.function: Carries hot, high-pressure vapour from the compressor to the condenser.
components.principle: Simple refrigerant pipe; the service port (illustrative) allows pressure measurement.
components.application: Present in every vapour compression system.
components.student: The hottest pipe in the system.

components.name: Liquid Line
components.subtitle: Copper tube, condenser → receiver/drier → expansion device
components.function: Carries high-pressure liquid refrigerant to the expansion device.
components.principle: Kept full of liquid so the expansion device is fed with liquid, not vapour.
components.application: Present in every vapour compression system.
components.student: A warm pipe filled with liquid refrigerant.

components.name: Suction Line (insulated)
components.subtitle: Evaporator → compressor
components.function: Returns low-pressure vapour from the evaporator to the compressor.
components.principle: Insulation limits unwanted heat gain and condensation on the cold pipe. The expansion valve's sensing bulb is clamped to this line.
components.cycleRole: Connects the refrigerating effect to compression.
components.application: Present in every vapour compression system.
components.student: The cold, fat, insulated pipe going back to the compressor.

components.name: Pressure Gauges
components.subtitle: Illustrative high-side (red) and low-side (blue) gauges — no readings shown
components.function: Indicate the high-side (condensing) and low-side (evaporating) pressures on a lab trainer.
components.principle: Bourdon-tube gauges deflect a needle in proportion to pressure.
components.cycleRole: Used in the lab to observe the cycle and compute performance from measured data.
components.student: Red = high-pressure side, blue = low-pressure side. Record the readings from your own rig.

components.name: Trainer Frame & Panel
components.subtitle: Base, aluminium uprights and mounting board
components.function: Supports and positions all components for demonstration.
components.principle: Rigid base with rubber feet; brackets hold the coils, valve and receiver.
components.cycleRole: Structural only — not part of the refrigerant circuit.
components.student: The board everything is mounted on.
